narrative.summary: Validators auto-pull a signed node binary with no public node source and no documented upgrade notice. Five validators labeled Hyper Foundation hold 47.98% of active stake, enough to halt but not to finalize alone.
narrative.detail: The repo reads the effective admin key as the binary signing key held by the core contributors, gated by validator adoption. No minimum upgrade notice is documented anywhere; a documented search on 2026-09-19 found none. At the 2026-09-16 read, 27 of 35 registered validators were active and the 5 Foundation-labeled ones count as 1 entity. The labels are self-set, so merging them is the conservative choice. The 4 entities needed for 2/3 hold only 0.04 points more than 2/3, so a small stake shift would make it 5 and raise the score. HyperCore reads rest on one operator's API.

reproduce.note: this RPC cannot replay the block of the build (it ignores the block tag, or no longer serves old state): the call reproduces the current value, not the one of the build; compare the composite and lastUpdated with this page

cheapest_fix.what: a stronger admin setup (admin power spread beyond one key, or checked by others)

main_gap.requirement: Admin power is not a bare key
main_gap.reason: One key, or a tiny group, can change it

independent_read.why: no code at this address on the chain's mainnet: a derived identifier for a native (non-EVM) entity such as HyperCore, or a contract that lives on another chain (a rollup's own L1 contracts); nothing for this reader to compare here
